text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Russia's Kazan aircraft factory and the Menatep bank have joined forces to start mass production of a new Tu-214 carrier powered by Rolls-Royce engines.
- Russian economy has posted a modest growth in the first quarter of 1997. The government and the Central Bank should tread very carefully not to break the encouraging trend.
- Uneximbank says it might have been a victim to unfair play by another major commercial bank in its strife to acquire a stake in the Sibneft oil company.
- Municipal authorities in St Petersburg are trying to tighten control over alcohol market to beef up the city budget.
- Russian mobile phone network operator Vympelkom says it will launch its new GSM-1800 system with a month's delay and will not cut prices to new subscribers.
- German telecom giant Siemens is not planning to bid for a stake in Russian telecommunications company Svyazinvest.
- The government is in a hurry to issue a new tranche of Russian Eurobonds to stake a place on the world financial markets.
- The plastic card operator Diners Club Russia has been given the right to serve the Diners Club card holders in Russia.
SEVODNYA

- Deputy Finance Minister Sergei Shatalov, widely regarded as father of the draft tax code, is doing his best to prevent the document from being transformed beyond recognition by numerous corrections and amendments.
- The board of directors of Sberbank is working to make good the damage done by the previous management.
- Federal Express courrier service in Russia cuts tariffs and increases volumes by 35 percent.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The government signles out seven major tasks on its agenda in an attempt to boost its popularity.
- The Constitutional Court rules that the customs officers have the right to seize illegally imported individual property.
- Russia may soon become a member of the G7 group as Japan is likely to drop its objections to such a move.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Khlystun in charge of agriculture says this sector is in urgent need of reform.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Former Acting Prime Minister Yegor Gaidar has been appointed member of an economic reform commission in the government.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
